---
title: "Blosc vs Zarr"
subtitle: "Picking a container format"
---

Both `write_blosc`/`read_blosc` and `write_zarr`/`read_zarr` encode with the exact
same codec (`encode_times` + Blosc(zstd, shuffle)) — compression ratio and fidelity
are the same either way. The choice is about the container, not the compression.

| | Blosc directory shard | Zarr |
|---|---|---|
| Dependency | `numcodecs` only | `numcodecs` + `zarr` |
| Metadata | hand-rolled `meta.json` | standard Zarr group attrs (`zarr.json`) |
| Interop | only readable via `spikepack.read_blosc` | any Zarr client (Python, JS, Julia, R) |
| Chunking | whole array in one block | can be chunked (`chunk_size=`) for partial/streaming reads |
| Multiple trains | one directory per train | can share one store as sibling groups (`group=`) |

**Use Blosc** for a minimal-dependency, self-contained archive of one train per
directory — e.g. shipping a single dataset release where every consumer already
uses this library.

**Use Zarr** when other tools need to read the data without this library, when you
want multiple recordings addressable in one store (`group="rec_a"`, `group="rec_b"`,
...), or when a single train is large enough that chunked/partial reads matter.

See the [benchmark](../explanation/benchmark.qmd) page for measured size and speed
differences across real recordings.
